harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured per-segment DHCP: node1 (VyOS) serves lan-a via eth2 (10.10.10.0/24, gateway 10.10.10.254) using Kea DHCPv4, and node2 (OPNsense) serves lan-b via vtnet2/opt1 (10.10.20.0/24, gateway 10.10.20.254) using dnsmasq (Kea was disabled on node2 after a port-67 bind conflict with the box's existing dnsmasq DHCP service on the default network). node3 obtains 10.10.10.100/24 from node1 with node1 as default route via eth1; node4 obtains 10.10.20.x/24 from node2 with node2 as default route via eth1. Ran the mandatory sequential single-node restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming changed boot identity and post-restart recovery of DHCP configuration/services and client leases/routes for each.
actions_performed: Mapped physical topology by testing IPs: node1 eth2 <-> node3 eth1 (lan-a) and node2 vtnet2 <-> node4 eth1 (lan-b), confirmed via ping/arping before committing real config
Configured VyOS node1 eth2=10.10.10.254/24 and Kea DHCPv4 shared-network LAN-A, subnet 10.10.10.0/24, pool 10.10.10.100-200, default-router 10.10.10.254; committed and saved

Configured OPNsense node2 new opt1 interface on vtnet2=10.10.20.254/24 via MVC Interfaces model; attempted Kea DHCPv4 for opt1 but hit a port-67 bind conflict with node2's existing dnsmasq DHCP service (used for the default network); disabled Kea on opt1 and instead added an opt1 DHCP range 10.10.20.100-200 to the existing Dnsmasq model, applied via configctl interface reconfigure / dnsmasq restart / filter reload
Configured node3 and node4 eth1 as DHCP clients in /etc/network/interfaces and verified they obtain addresses and default routes from their respective front routers
Captured pre-restart boot identity (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD) and health evidence for all 4 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time via native reboot mechanisms, polling exec availability after each before proceeding to the next node
Verified changed boot identity and full recovery (DHCP service/config and client lease+route) after each individual node restart

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) hands node3 an address from its own lan-a pool with itself as default route
evidence.summary: node1 eth2 configured to 10.10.10.254/24 with Kea DHCPv4 subnet 10.10.10.0/24; node3 eth1 obtains 10.10.10.100/24 via DHCP with default route via 10.10.10.254

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) hands node4 an address from its own lan-b pool with itself as default route
evidence.summary: node2 opt1/vtnet2 configured to 10.10.20.254/24 with dnsmasq DHCP range 10.10.20.100-200; node4 eth1 obtains a lease (10.10.20.137/24) via DHCP with default route via 10.10.20.254, persisted through dhcpcd restart

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline boot identity and health before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id e98d9010-e1da-463d-bb8b-b401e38f9894 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged, node became unreachable, then returned with new boot_id 0ea6dcd2-9582-4330-ab9a-7fa358c23b92

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of DHCP service and lan-a config
evidence.summary: isc-kea-dhcp4-server active and eth2=10.10.10.254/24 persisted after reboot; node3 still able to ping node1 gateway

evidence.summary: Captured node2 kern.boottime Sun Sep 6 04:34:20 2026 prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged, SSH transport became unreachable, then node returned with new kern.boottime Sun Sep 6 04:57:52 2026

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of DHCP service and lan-b config
evidence.summary: vtnet2/opt1=10.10.20.254/24 and dnsmasq DHCP range for opt1 persisted after reboot, dnsmasq process running; node4 lease/route to node2 still intact

evidence.summary: eth1 re-obtained 10.10.20.137/24 via DHCP with default route via 10.10.20.254 after reboot
